raw_response.blind_rationale: Blind reading of Li, McManus, & Cronk (2025) shows a cross-sectional analysis of N = 11,065 rural/community Afridev hand-pump water points in Liberia (2017 national WASH water-point census) examining operational, technical, management, and fee-collection determinants of binary pump functionality. On Narrow Criterion 2, the study sits on the governance/tariff boundary ('borderline_governance_or_proxy'): its headline governance predictor ('Maintainer': Local [lumping NGO, community, local group, and private owner], Institutional [school, health facilities, other], and WASH Committee vs. No Management) captures operational O&M management structure rather than a formal legal or statutory rule, while a secondary predictor ('Payment Status': volumetric fee, flat rate, or post-breakdown collection vs. free water, with 30% [2,539] imputed missingness) measures local user-fee/tariff rules primarily as an O&M financing mechanism alongside physical/technical predictors (damage status, repair time, mechanic/toolkit availability, and spare-parts distance). On Criterion 4, binary hand-pump functionality ('Yes—Functional [in use or not in use]' vs. 'No—Broken down') directly measures community water-point service reliability/operational availability in a setting where 39% of the population relies on hand pumps ('yes_household_or_service_access'), although the unit of analysis is the physical water point rather than the household and 'functional (but not in use)' is coded as functional. For SWiM classification, the primary management-regime estimates (Institutional aOR = 2.893, Local aOR = 3.733, WASH Committee aOR = 2.426 vs. No Management) and technical-capacity estimate (mechanic with toolkit aOR = 1.246) map most closely to Family C (ownership, regulation, institutional capacity, administrative structure), though lumping private owners, NGOs, and community groups into 'Local' blurs pure ownership/administrative lines; conversely, if the review extracted the user-fee/tariff contrasts ('By Volume vs. Free' aOR = 0.886; 'Flat rate vs. Free' aOR = 0.847; 'After a system breakdown vs. Free' aOR = 1.336), tariff/cost-recovery modalities do not fit cleanly into Families A, B, or C unless Family C encompasses tariff rules, which would explain a reasoned non-fit if tariff structure rather than management regime was the target row. Notably, the paper also contains multiple text-vs-table reporting discrepancies (e.g., p. 9 claims no payment category was significant while citing p = 0.011 for post-breakdown payment in Table 5; p. 7 cites unadjusted OR/CI values while discussing adjusted results; Table 5 mislabels 'Always Water vs. Seasonal' as 'Seasonal vs. Year-Around').

raw_response.headline_estimate_summary: Multivariable logistic regression (N = 11,065 Afridev hand pumps; Functional = 9,089, Non-functional = 1,976; Table 5, PDF p. 8; mutually adjusted for water point maintenance, repair time, mechanic & toolkit availability, damage status, payment status, water availability, and spare-parts supplier distance): (1) Water point maintenance (ref: No Management): Local vs. No Management aOR = 3.733 (Wald 95% CI: 2.993–4.657, p < 0.0001; unadjusted OR = 4.730, 95% CI: 3.950–5.665); Institutional vs. No Management aOR = 2.893 (95% CI: 2.349–3.562, p < 0.0001; unadjusted OR = 3.274, 95% CI: 2.770–3.869); WASH Committee vs. No Management aOR = 2.426 (95% CI: 1.946–3.026, p < 0.0001; unadjusted OR = 2.657, 95% CI: 2.248–3.140). (2) Payment Status (ref: Free): By Volume vs. Free aOR = 0.886 (95% CI: 0.552–1.421, p = 0.614; unadjusted OR = 1.294, p = 0.195); Flat rate vs. Free aOR = 0.847 (95% CI: 0.634–1.133, p = 0.263; unadjusted OR = 0.848, p = 0.177); After a system breakdown vs. Free aOR = 1.336 (95% CI: 1.066–1.673, p = 0.011; unadjusted OR = 1.084, p = 0.408). (3) Mechanic & toolkit availability (ref: no mechanic): Mechanic with toolkit aOR = 1.246 (95% CI: 1.084–1.431, p = 0.002); Mechanic without toolkit aOR = 0.896 (95% CI: 0.726–1.106, p = 0.307). (4) Bayesian Network scenario simulation (PDF pp. 10–11): 'most ideal' (Local management, repair <1 week, mechanic with toolkit; P = 77.7%) vs. 'least ideal' (No Management, repair >1 year, no mechanic; P = 45.5%) yielded Posterior Odds Ratio (POR) = 4.19 (no SEs reported; Wald 95% CIs reported in Table 5).
raw_response.study_design_and_sample: Cross-sectional observational study of national water-point census data (2017 WASH-Liberia survey across all 15 counties in Liberia; 20,205 mapped water points, restricted to improved water points equipped with Afridev hand pumps). Unit of analysis: individual Afridev hand-pump water point. Primary analytic sample: N = 11,065 Afridev hand pumps (9,089 functional and 1,976 non-functional), analyzed via univariable/multivariable logistic regression (with hot-deck Approximated Bayesian Bootstrap single imputation for missing values) and Bayesian network modeling (80% training / 20% testing split).
